title: Grateful Dead Live at P.N.E. Coliseum on 1973-06-22
lineage: AUDMC > Reel > Reel > CD > DAT > WAV > SHN recorded by Donn Amick, FOB, Sony EMC mics spread out across the row > TC-126 master cassette > Amick's Reel recorded at 7-1/2ips > Matt Williams' Reel at 3-3/4ips w/ Dolby(Teac AN-60)

ai_review.summary: Stunning 1973 audience recording capturing a high‑energy show highlighted by a legendary Bird Song and an explosive He's Gone/48 Chambers jam, with excellent stereo warmth despite minor early dropouts.
ai_review.review: This audience tape delivers one of the most celebrated 1973 shows – a smoking setlist packed with a rapturous Bird Song, a monster He's Gone → 48 Chambers of Phil sequence and killer renditions of Looks Like Rain, Race Is On and Row Jimmy. The stereo ambience is rich and warm, sounding almost as good as a soundboard, though the opening of Bertha fades in and there are occasional tape‑hiss/cut‑out moments. Overall the performance is high‑energy and the recording quality makes it a must‑listen for Deadheads.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews are 5‑star, praising both the musical performance and the audience recording; only a few note minor technical glitches, so the combined show (70%) + recording (30%) rating is very high.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Perfect stereo image and warm room ambience; occasional early fade‑in on Bertha, brief mono segment at the start of Here Comes Sunshine, some tape hiss and occasional cut‑outs, but overall crisp and richly detailed.

standout_songs: He's Gone > 48 Chambers of Phil > Ecstasy > Bliss > Terror > Amazement Jam
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows seamlessly with a monster second‑set jam that builds from He's Gone into the 48 Chambers of Phil suite, punctuated by tight transitions and plenty of space for improvisation; the audience tape captures the room’s natural dynamics.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers laud Jerry's soulful soloing, inspired playing throughout the show and his “incredibly soulful” guitar tone.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil is praised for a powerful re‑emergence in the jam (the Phil Zone) and for delivering a tight, energetic bass line during the 48 Chambers sequence.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s keyboard work gets special mention – “Chick Corea‑esque circles” and overall stellar playing that drives the jams.
